source.title: DeepLoop: Depth Scaling for Looped Transformers
source.authors: Shu-Zhen Li; Yi-Fan Zhang; Jia-Cheng Guo; Quanquan Gu; Meng-Di Wang

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present, including appendices; no truncation or formatting issue prevents extraction.
record.tranche_reason: The paper tests how residual scaling affects training in looped Transformers and reports both successful and failed training outcomes across scaling exponents. This refines the broader training claim to a tied-depth Transformer setting and finds that outcomes depend on the exponent and loop count.
record.gate_note: Own results bearing on the versions are the GPT-2 validation-loss comparison, downstream accuracy comparisons, ARC-AGI accuracy comparison, and the exponent p-sweep training/escape outcomes. Theoretical derivations and cited findings are not rows. Validation and downstream rows do not measure training classification error, so they do not bear on V1. The paper does not test V2, V3, V4, V5, or V6 as stated.
record.test_reason: The study tests residual parameterization in looped, normalized Transformers, not any listed version. It does not measure CIFAR training classification error, teacher-student local minima, plain-network depth degradation, activation-matched initialization in plain networks, learning-rate stability thresholds, or batch-normalization benefits. The exponent sweep jointly changes skip scaling and initialization gain; it does not isolate V4's initialization mechanism.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate but omits the main conditional theoretical result and HRM evidence. The authors derive p≥1/2 for a bounded first-order perturbation bound under worst-case aligned visits at fixed physical depth, recovering p≥1/4 for decorrelated visits. They report validation-loss gains with looping, mostly favorable downstream averages, and improved HRM ARC-AGI accuracy. The short p-sweep brackets a gradual transition near 1/2; it does not establish reliable training at exactly 1/2 or directly measure visit alignment.
record.recipe_differences: The experiments compare a modern pre-LN looped baseline with a post-normalized sandwich block using DeepLoop scaling; the p-sweep holds the sandwich block fixed and varies only p. These language-model and reasoning recipes do not match the original CIFAR classification-training methods.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcome varies with loop count R and residual-scaling exponent p. In the p-sweep at R=3, escape fractions rise with p; the transition is gradual and every seed escapes only from p=0.55 upward. Downstream average at R=5 is lower for DeepLoop in the medium 1-shot condition.

fits_no_version.finding: DeepLoop matches the pre-LN baseline at R=1 and lowers final validation loss at R=3, 5, and 7 at both GPT-2 scales in single-seed runs. The comparison changes normalization placement as well as residual and initialization scaling.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The complete DeepLoop parameterization improves validation loss over the tested pre-LN looped Transformer baseline when blocks are revisited.

fits_no_version.finding: Medium-scale downstream averages favor DeepLoop at activated loop counts except 1-shot R=5, where it scores 54.19% versus 54.42%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Downstream benefits of DeepLoop depend on loop count and evaluation condition.

fits_no_version.finding: DeepLoop HRM improves ARC-AGI-1 voted accuracy at all five budgets, including 36.50% to 39.75% at K=2.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: DeepLoop residual parameterization improves the tested HRM's ARC-AGI-1 evaluation accuracy.

fits_no_version.finding: At R=3, pooled any-attempt escape counts rise from 0/5 at p=0.30 to 5/5 at p=0.55 and 0.60; p=0.50 reaches 3/5. Among plotted successful attempts, mean validation loss rises from 3.70 at p=0.45 to 3.80 at p=0.60.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In this short-horizon looped Transformer experiment, stronger residual scaling increases reliability of escape from the unigram floor while reducing learning progress conditional on success.

record.problems: The main language-model comparisons are single-seed and the authors say multi-seed runs are needed to quantify run-to-run variance. The p-sweep covers one scale, one loop depth, and a short optimizer-step budget; the authors state that the transition is gradual rather than sharp. Reported language-model measures are validation loss and downstream accuracy, not training classification error.
record.rows_left_out: The paper also gives task-level downstream accuracies in Table 2 and Table 4. They are not individually extracted because those evaluations measure transfer accuracy rather than any claim-version outcome, and the aggregate rows already record the reported comparison relevant to the paper's result. No claim version had a qualifying row.

untested.parts: All: convolutional-network training classification error on CIFAR-10/100, including random labels and model-size or training-recipe qualifications.
All: two-layer ReLU teacher-student local minima and the effect of extra student neurons.
All: plain versus residual convolutional-network training error with increasing depth, deep plain tanh initialization, and normalization-free Fixup training.
All: activation-matched initialization preserving signals and gradients in plain networks, learning-speed and trainable-depth comparisons, and orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization.
All: learning rates relative to the initial linearized stability limit, catapult recovery, curvature evolution, and edge-of-stability dynamics.
All: batch-normalization effects on training speed and tolerated learning rates, and Fixup comparisons without normalization.

record.verdict_notes: The record's tests/T5 designation contradicts its correctly unlinked rows. These method-performance comparisons should remain contextual findings rather than evidence rows for V1–V6. A residual-scaling exponent threshold is distinct from V5's learning-rate stability threshold. No omitted result qualifies for a listed version.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, random or corrupted labels, SGD/Adam, model-size comparisons and early stopping are not tested.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems and spurious local minima are not tested.
Plain versus shortcut networks and depth-dependent training error are not compared.
Activation-matched initializations and their effects on plain-network learning speed or trainable depth are not tested.
The study does not test learning rates above a stability limit, curvature changes, or edge-of-stability behavior.
Batch normalization is not tested; experiments use RMSNorm, and no comparison isolates normalization's speed or learning-rate effects.
